exposure: psychosomatic interventions (stress management, relaxation techniques, counseling)
outcome: neonatal outcomes (intrauterine distress, premature birth, asphyxia)
cohort: A total of 200 pregnant women diagnosed with gestational hypertension, divided into a control group receiving only pharmacological treatment and a case group receiving standard care plus psychosomatic medicine.
finding: Psychosomatic interventions significantly improved microbiome diversity, reduced pro-inflammatory cytokines, lowered blood pressure, enhanced psychological well-being, decreased complications, and resulted in better neonatal and delivery outcomes for pregnant women with gestational hypertension.
mod_finding: The case group demonstrated significant improvements in delivery outcomes (P = 0.032), with mode of delivery being a measured primary outcome.
